label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 4
knowledgePattern: Separate decreasing height, derivative sign, signed area and bending
solution:
A nonincreasing polynomial has derivative at most zero throughout the interval, so statement 2 is necessary. At an endpoint this also follows from continuity of the polynomial derivative and its signs in the interior.

Statement 1 need not hold: the constant polynomial f(x) = 1 is nonincreasing but has equal endpoint values. The same polynomial refutes statement 3 because its integral over a nonempty forward interval is positive.

For statement 4 take f(x)=x2 on [−1,0]. It is decreasing there, but f(−1)+f(0)=1>2f(−1/2)=1/2. Thus only 2 is necessary. Answer C.

hints.body: Use the supplied definition to determine what it allows at equal heights and what it implies about gradients.
hints.recap: The sign of the derivative describes the direction of change of a differentiable function.
hints.pitfall: Nonincreasing need not mean strictly decreasing.
hints.pause: Test the first two statements, including a constant polynomial.
